title: UnitedHealth is down about 10% on a Medicare audit proposal that isn'teven final. Overreaction, or the start of something worse?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[UNH\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/UNH/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/UNH/)) dropped 7.8% in the midday  
write-up, from Tuesday's close of $389.68 to $359.29, extending a  
two-session decline to roughly -13% and touching a seven-week low.  
Later prints were closer to -10% to -11%, around $347–$350, so treat  
the blog figure as stale.  
  
The selloff accelerated on the CMS "CRUSH" proposal unveiled Nov. 16.  
It would extrapolate Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment audit findings  
from samples across entire contracts back to payment year 2018 and  
drop the fee-for-service adjuster. CMS estimates roughly $9 billion in  
industry clawbacks per payment year, and UnitedHealth, the largest MA  
insurer, has not sized its exposure. The rule is a proposal, not a  
final regulation.  
  
Write-up on why \[UNH\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/UNH/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/UNH/)) sold off  
today, including the CMS estimates and the two-session slide:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-unitedhealth-group-unh-stock-down-7-80-today-40552/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-unitedhealth-group-unh-stock-down-7-80-today-40552/)  
  
Is this a real margin threat, or is the tape overreacting to a rule  
that isn't final and could still be challenged?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's write-up, not live  
quotes, and the price has already moved further.
